entry.title: Web Bluetooth: BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.maxWriteWithoutResponseSize
entry.content:
Specification title

Web Bluetooth: BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.maxWriteWithoutResponseSize

Specification or proposal URL

whatwg/bluetooth#672 (open spec PR; published spec: https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/)

Proposal author(s)

@hjanuschka

web-feature id

web-bluetooth

Caniuse.com URL

https://caniuse.com/web-bluetooth

Bugzilla URL

https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1204396

WebKit standards-position

Not filed -- WebKit is opposed to Web Bluetooth overall.

Other information

Adds one attribute and one event to BluetoothRemoteGATTServer:

partial interface BluetoothRemoteGATTServer {
  readonly attribute unsigned short maxWriteWithoutResponseSize;
  attribute EventHandler onmaxwritewithoutresponsesizechanged;
};
  • Value is ATT_MTU - 3 (write command header), so 20 before any MTU exchange.
  • Set on connect, updated only when the UA observes an MTU change, which also fires maxwritewithoutresponsesizechanged. The event carries no data; listeners read the attribute.

Why: pages can't tell how big a single write may be. Over ATT_MTU - 3 bytes, writeValueWithoutResponse() either fails or is silently truncated depending on platform. So apps hard-code 20 bytes/packet even though modern links negotiate 247+ (crbug.com/40265040, crbug.com/40686244, crbug.com/40163619).

Privacy: one integer from a device the user picked in the chooser. No new prompt, no new capability, no cross-session state, only readable while that origin's GATT connection is open.

Status: nothing shipped yet. Chromium CL is in review, not landed (crrev.com/c/7879985); spec PR open; Intent to Ship pending with the API owners (ChromeStatus, would target M160 behind a killswitch). No WPT yet.

Not asking Firefox to revisit its Web Bluetooth position (#95, #364) or implement the API -- just whether this addition's shape is acceptable before more engines build on it. That said, I also contribute to Gecko, so if there is interest I'm happy to do the Firefox-side work myself as a follow-up.

Other information

This request is specifically for the WebTransportOptions.congestionControl constructor option and the read-only WebTransport.congestionControl attribute, rather than WebTransport as a whole.

The API allows applications to request "default", "throughput", or "low-latency" congestion-control behavior. These values are implementation-defined hints rather than selections of named algorithms. If a requested optimization is unsupported, the specification permits and requires the effective value to fall back to "default".

Related broader WebTransport position: #167

entry.title: The focusreset event
entry.content:
Specification title

The focusreset event

Specification or proposal URL (if available)

whatwg/html#13050

Explainer URL (if available)

https://github.com/noamr/explainers/blob/main/focusreset-explainer.md

Proposal author(s)

@noamr

web-feature id

No response

MDN URL

mdn/mdn#876

Caniuse.com URL

No response

Bugzilla URL

https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2081188

Mozillians who can provide input

@zcorpan @smaug----

WebKit standards-position

WebKit/standards-positions#732

Other information

When the currently focused element in a document (or one of its ancestors) is removed from the DOM, the HTML Standard's node-remove focus fixup rule synchronously resets the document's focused area to its viewport (document.body / document.documentElement) without firing blur or focusout.

Because no event is fired when focus is lost due to DOM removal, UI component libraries, modal focus traps, and keyboard navigation tools currently rely on expensive or fragile workarounds such as attaching a MutationObserver({ childList: true, subtree: true }) to document.body (e.g., Radix UI's FocusScope, focus-trap) or polling document.activeElement via setInterval (e.g., Material UI's FocusTrap, Tridactyl).

This proposal introduces a focusreset event (and onfocusreset event handler IDL attribute) on Document. When a focused element is removed from a document that has focus—resetting focus to the viewport—a focus reset is signaled for that document. In the mutation observer microtask checkpoint (notify mutation observers, immediately after MutationObserver callbacks and slotchange events), if focus has not been explicitly moved to another element and the document still has focus, a focusreset event is fired at Document.

Specification PRs, Issue & Tests:

  • Issue: whatwg/html#12842
  • HTML PR: whatwg/html#13050
  • DOM PR: whatwg/dom#1512
  • WPT PR: web-platform-tests/wpt#63595

entry.title: Sealed form fields (`<sealedinput>` and the `sealed-fields` CSP directive)
entry.content:

Proposal author(s)

@decleezy

No response

Caniuse.com URL

No response

Bugzilla URL

No response

Mozillians who can provide input

No response

WebKit standards-position

WebKit/standards-positions#730

Other information

A form control whose value is HPKE-encrypted in the browser to a key published by the form's destination (/.well-known/sealed-input), so page script, extensions, session replay, and intermediaries see only ciphertext. A companion sealed-fields CSP directive seals ordinary inputs by autocomplete token. It generalizes the shape already shipped in Apple Pay JS and the Digital Credentials API to arbitrary sensitive fields (identifiers, secrets, health data).

There is a polyfill and a native implementation in Ladybird (13 patches with engine tests); one server opens envelopes from both. The native work's list of plaintext side channels we closed is here: https://github.com/madeit-build/koschei/blob/main/docs/research/native-feasibility-ladybird.md

We'd especially value Mozilla's view on whether the explainer's answer to the decoy-field objection (which ended writeonly in 2014) is sufficient, and on side channels the deviations list misses.

The WebAssembly Component Model is a proposal at the W3C WebAssembly CG/WG. A wasm component has a high level typed API that can be used by languages like JS. A wasm component implements the high level API using a bundle of wasm modules along with an ABI for passing values.

Mozilla is experimenting with this as a way to improve performance for users and simplify the experience for developers when using wasm.

It's a phase 1 proposal in the Wasm CG. Mozilla is contributing to the proposal, and prototyping an implementation.

entry.title: HTML: Allow activation of a checked radio button to clear it
entry.content:
Specification title

HTML: Allow activation of a checked radio button to clear it

Specification or proposal URL (if available)

whatwg/html#12480

Explainer URL (if available)

whatwg/html#12480

Proposal author(s)

@hjanuschka

web-feature id

None.

MDN URL

None.

Caniuse.com URL

None.

Bugzilla URL

Not yet filed.

Mozillians who can provide input

None identified.

WebKit standards-position

WebKit/standards-positions#721

Other information

The proposal changes radio-button activation so that activating the currently checked radio button can return an optional radio group to its no-selection state. If the group has a radio button with a checked content attribute, activation instead restores that author-provided default.

The use case is an optional form question where a user accidentally selects an answer and currently has no native way to return the group to its initial no-selection state. Radio groups already support no selection initially and through script; the proposal makes that state reachable through user activation.

Demo: https://static.januschka.com/i-40761596/index.html

Chromium tracking issue: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40761596
